data.title: Resolve & Send via Local MCP
data.goalStatement: The handoff itself: toolbar staged-annotation counter, 'Clear' action, and the primary 'Resolve & Send' button (disabled at zero staged annotations and while a send is in flight). On send, Rectify packages the full frame screenshot, per-annotation crops, view-hierarchy XML dump and generated prompt into a versioned payload envelope and transmits it to the locally running Claude Code agent through the existing local 'rectify' MCP server for retrieval via a get_latest_annotation-style tool — the sole transport in v1, no file or webhook fallback. During send a status sequence (Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent) animates with colored dots, then a toast confirms 'Sent N annotations… · <time>s' with an 'Open session' link; afterwards live mirroring resumes automatically and the counter resets to 0. All data stays local; typical localhost sends complete in under ~2s. Why: this is GOAL-4 and the point where everything captured becomes actionable for the agent; research notes MCP tool naming and payload schema should be deliberate design, since Aki's near-identical tool surface already exists for desktop.

functionalRequirements.text: In the toolbar, show a staged-annotation counter, a 'Clear' action that removes all staged annotations, and a primary 'Resolve & Send' button that is disabled while zero annotations are staged or while a send is in progress.

On 'Resolve & Send', package the full frame screenshot, per-annotation crops, view-hierarchy XML dump, and generated prompt, and transmit them to the locally running Claude Code agent via the local 'rectify' MCP server (e.g. for retrieval through a `get_latest_annotation`-style tool).

During send, show a visible status sequence (Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent) with colored dots, then confirm with a toast ('Sent N annotations to Claude Code · frame + hierarchy · <time>s') including an 'Open session' link.
After a successful send, resume live mirroring automatically and reset the staged-annotation counter to 0.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Resolve & Send payload transmission to the local MCP server should typically complete in under ~2s on localhost for a typical batch.
All mirror stream data, screenshots, hierarchy dumps, and payloads stay local to the machine; no network egress beyond localhost MCP communication.
The payload format (prompt + crops + hierarchy XML) is versioned so the receiving MCP server/Claude Code agent can evolve its parsing without breaking older sends.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given zero annotations are staged, then 'Resolve & Send' is disabled; given one or more are staged, it is enabled; 'Clear' removes all staged annotations and resets the counter to 0.

When the user clicks 'Resolve & Send', then the frame screenshot, per-annotation crops, hierarchy XML, and generated prompt are transmitted via the local MCP server such that a Claude Code session calling the retrieval tool receives the complete payload.

When sending, then the status sequence Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent displays in order with colored dots, and on completion a toast shows the sent-count/time summary with an 'Open session' link.
While a send is in progress, 'Resolve & Send' is disabled and only re-enables after the toast confirms or the send fails.
After a successful send, then live mirroring resumes automatically and the staged-annotation counter resets to 0.
Given a staged annotation batch is sent, then the persisted payload envelope carries an explicit format/schema version field that the receiving MCP server can read to select its parsing path.

userStories.iWant: one 'Resolve & Send' action that delivers the whole batch to my running Claude Code session over the local rectify MCP server
userStories.soThat: the agent can start fixing with full context and zero copy-paste
